newsitem.title: USA: Ted Turner says cult suicide good end for "nuts".
newsitem.headline: Ted Turner says cult suicide good end for "nuts".

text.p: Outspoken Time Warner Vice Chairman and Atlanta Braves owner Ted Turner Saturday called the mass suicide in California "a good way to get rid of a few nuts."

"There are too many nuts running around anyway, right?" Turner told reporters at a clubhouse news conference before the first professional exhibition baseball game at Turner Field. The stadium built for the 1996 Summer Olympics has been converted for use by the Braves and is named after the broadcasting executive.

"It's a good way to get rid of a few nuts, you know, you gotta look at it that way," he said of the Heaven's Gate cult suicide. "Well, they did it peacefully. At least they didn't do like these S.O.B.s that go to McDonald's or post offices and shoot a lot of innocent people and then shoot themselves. At least they went out and just did it to themselves."
Turner said he was trying to look at the bright side of the suicide by 39 people. "Turning on the TV, all it is is one murder after another. There's hardly ever anything good," he said.

"You know, 29 people, 39 people committed suicide to go up to the comet. Well, what about the other six billion that didn't, you know? That's a small percentage, 39 out of six billion," he said. "That comet does look good. I've been looking at it. I would kinda to go up there myself. I mean, is it that much different from other religions that say you're going to heaven?"
Turner also said he agreed with fans who were upset at increased concession stand prices and a policy that fans cannot bring food and drink into the new stadium.
"Well, it's just the way it is, you know. They can bring it in in their tummies, eat it on the way down here if they want to," he said. "And we got free water don't we? We got water fountains."
When told by Braves president Stan Kasten that a Coca-Cola soft drink would cost $3.50, Turner responded, "Are you serious?"

"That's outrageous," Turner said. "I think the fans are right. But they don't have to buy it and I won't and they shouldn't either. I'm drinking water. I'm not gonna drink, not at $3.50, that's too much."
